stem: Used needles and bandages from a clinic are an example of which type of waste?

stem: Which step comes **first** in the waste hierarchy?

options.rationale: Correct: avoiding waste is best.
Recycling comes after reducing and reusing.
Disposal is the last resort.
Incineration is a disposal or recovery method.

explanation: The hierarchy is reduce, reuse, recycle, recover, then dispose: avoiding waste comes first.

stem: How can plastic litter cause flooding in towns?

options.content: It absorbs rainwater and swells up
options.rationale: Plastic does not absorb water.
Litter does not change rainfall.

options.rationale: Correct: blocked drains overflow.

options.rationale: Plastic does not melt in rivers.

stem: Which is the **strongest** criticism of relying only on landfills to manage waste?

options.rationale: This is not a criticism, and it is not true.

options.content: They make recycling compulsory for everyone
options.rationale: Landfills have no effect of this kind.

options.content: They can only hold medical waste

stem: Explain **three** roles of citizens in waste management.

points.description: Identifies reducing and reusing
Develops: less waste is produced, so less needs collecting
Identifies using bins / not littering, burning or dumping
Develops: streets and drains stay clean; less pollution
Identifies taking part in clean-ups / recycling / reporting illegal dumping / paying rates
Develops: e.g. rates fund collection; reports help EMA and councils act

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Citizens can reduce and reuse, for example by carrying cloth bags, so less waste needs collecting. They should put rubbish in bins and never burn or dump it, which keeps streets and drains clean. They can take part in clean-ups and report illegal dumping, which helps the council and EMA act against offenders.

explanation: One mark for each role and one for its development.
hints: What can each person do before, during and after waste is made?

stem: Suggest **two** ways a fictional rural district council near Marondera could improve waste management at a growing business centre, and explain how each would help.

points.description: Suggests providing skips/bins and a regular collection day
Explains that waste is not left to pile up, so burning and dumping fall
Suggests separating waste for composting and recycling / by-laws with fines / awareness for traders
Explains how it reduces the waste to be disposed of or changes behaviour

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The council could place skips at the business centre and collect them on a fixed day each week, so rubbish does not pile up and traders no longer burn it. It could also ask traders to separate organic waste for a compost site and plastic for a recycler, which reduces the amount of waste the council must dispose of.

explanation: One mark for each suitable way and one for its explanation.

stem:
**Source A** — a report in a fictional town newsletter, Midlands Province, 2026 (invented for this question)

> Residents of Ward 7 say refuse trucks came only twice in the past three months. Heaps of rubbish now stand at every street corner. Some residents burn the heaps at night; others dump bags in the stream behind the market. The council says it has only two working trucks for the whole town. A group of young people has started collecting plastic bottles and selling them to a recycler.

Read Source A and answer the questions.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: According to the source, what is the council's explanation for the problem?

options.rationale: This is not mentioned in the source.

options.content: it has too few working trucks
options.rationale: Correct: only two trucks for the whole town.

options.content: the recycler buys too many bottles
options.rationale: Recycling is not blamed.

Dumping bags in the stream (water pollution)

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Explain whether the young people's recycling project can solve the ward's waste problem.

points.description: It helps: removes some plastic and earns income
But it deals only with one material (plastic bottles), not food or other waste

stem: This question is about approaches to waste management.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Describe the roles of local authorities, EMA and businesses in waste management.

points.description: Local authorities: collect refuse, provide bins/skips
run disposal sites and enforce by-laws
EMA: sets standards, licenses waste sites and hazardous waste handlers
inspects, educates and fines offenders / bans polluting products
Businesses: manage their own industrial waste safely
reduce packaging and take part in recycling

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Local authorities collect refuse, provide bins and skips, run disposal sites and enforce by-laws against dumping. EMA sets standards for waste disposal, licenses waste sites and handlers of hazardous waste, inspects them, educates the public and fines offenders. Businesses must manage their own industrial waste safely, reduce packaging and take part in recycling.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: "Recycling is the best answer to Zimbabwe's waste problem." Discuss.

points.description: For recycling: saves materials and energy, reduces dumped waste, creates income and jobs
Limits: not all materials have buyers; collection systems limited; organic waste and e-waste need other methods
Other approaches: reduce and reuse (higher in hierarchy), composting, regular collection, managed landfills
Supported judgement

levels.descriptor: Developed explanation of several relevant points or arguments, supported by accurate, specific knowledge and examples, considering more than one side and reaching a supported judgement that answers the question.
Developed explanation of some factors or arguments with relevant supporting detail; a judgement is attempted but is only partly supported, or the other side is thin.
Some explanation of one or two relevant factors, or several points described with limited explanation; little or no judgement.
Simple, general or narrative statements with limited relevance to the question; little explanation.

answerSpec.modelAnswer:
Recycling has clear benefits. It turns plastic, paper, glass and metal into new products, saves raw materials and energy, reduces the waste sent to dumps and gives income to collectors and small businesses.

But recycling has limits. Not every material has a buyer, collection points are few, and much household waste is food and garden waste, which cannot be recycled in this way. E-waste and medical waste need special handling.

Other approaches matter as much or more. Reducing and reusing come higher in the waste hierarchy because they avoid waste altogether. Composting suits the large share of organic waste. Regular collection and managed landfills are still needed for what remains.

I disagree that recycling is the best answer on its own. It is a valuable part of the solution, but Zimbabwe's waste problem needs reduction, composting, collection and recycling working together.

explanation: A practice evaluative item on waste management approaches.
hints: In (b), use the waste hierarchy to weigh recycling against other steps.
